findings.quote: Water enters the town through a treatment plant. Filters remove small particles before the water reaches storage tanks. Pipes then carry it to homes. The town website has a written description of this route. Residents may visit the plant during its open house.

lesson-comprehension-skills-authors-purp.quote: What is the author's main purpose?

lesson-comprehension-skills-authors-purp.quote: Which purpose is dominant: explaining a process or persuading residents to visit?

lesson-comprehension-skills-authors-purp.quote: **Syntax** means how words and sentence parts are arranged.

reading-comprehension-comprehension-skil.quote: Each paragraph has a job. It may introduce a claim, give evidence, explain a cause, answer an objection, or propose a response.
reading-comprehension-comprehension-skil.note: Reference resolution and paragraph functions are taught. Example #11 compares the main problem/solution pattern with embedded cause/effect and comparison.

reading-comprehension-comprehension-skil.quote: Collect the writer's claims, reasons, examples, and repeated judgments.
reading-comprehension-comprehension-skil.note: Argument position is distinguished from story narration. Example #9 weighs both sides and identifies a qualified trial position.

reading-comprehension-comprehension-skil.quote: A writer may select only helpful evidence, frame a group unfairly, or leave out important facts.
reading-comprehension-comprehension-skil.note: Selection, framing, omission, and fair viewpoint versus bias are explained and diagnosed in example #10.

reading-comprehension-comprehension-skil.quote: Use these sentence clues with the whole passage when judging purpose or viewpoint.
reading-comprehension-comprehension-skil.note: Voice, reported speech, agreement, parallelism, modals, modifiers, conditionals, and complete sentences are taught; example #12 applies the combined clues.
